import pandas as pd
from sqlalchemy import text

# First, let's compute the bounding box and create Voronoi cells
# We'll use ST_VoronoiPolygons on the collection of all station points
query = text("""
WITH stations AS (
    SELECT id, coordinate
    FROM air_quality_station
),
station_collection AS (
    SELECT ST_Collect(coordinate) as geom FROM air_quality_station
),
bbox AS (
    SELECT ST_Envelope(ST_Collect(coordinate)) as geom FROM air_quality_station
),
voronoi AS (
    SELECT 
        (ST_Dump(ST_VoronoiPolygons(sc.geom))).geom as cell_geom,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER () as cell_id
    FROM station_collection sc
),
-- Match each Voronoi cell to its generating station by finding which station is contained in each cell
cell_station AS (
    SELECT 
        v.cell_id,
        v.cell_geom,
        s.id as station_id
    FROM voronoi v
    JOIN stations s ON ST_Contains(v.cell_geom, s.coordinate)
),
-- Clip each cell to the bounding box
clipped_cells AS (
    SELECT 
        cs.station_id,
        ST_Intersection(cs.cell_geom, b.geom) as clipped_geom
    FROM cell_station cs, bbox b
)
-- Calculate geodesic area in km² for each station's cell
SELECT 
    station_id,
    ST_Area(clipped_geom::geography) / 1000000.0 as area_km2
FROM clipped_cells
ORDER BY station_id
""")

cell_areas = pd.read_sql(query, engine)
print(cell_areas)

# Sum areas for roadside stations (14, 16, 17)
roadside_stations = [14, 16, 17]
roadside_total = cell_areas[cell_areas['station_id'].isin(roadside_stations)]['area_km2'].sum()
print(f"\nTotal area for roadside stations (14, 16, 17): {roadside_total:.1f} km²")

import pandas as pd
from sqlalchemy import text

# Fix: Cast geography to geometry for spatial operations
query = text("""
WITH stations AS (
    SELECT id, coordinate::geometry as geom
    FROM air_quality_station
),
station_collection AS (
    SELECT ST_Collect(geom) as geom FROM stations
),
bbox AS (
    SELECT ST_Envelope(ST_Collect(geom)) as geom FROM stations
),
voronoi AS (
    SELECT 
        (ST_Dump(ST_VoronoiPolygons(sc.geom))).geom as cell_geom,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER () as cell_id
    FROM station_collection sc
),
-- Match each Voronoi cell to its generating station by finding which station is contained in each cell
cell_station AS (
    SELECT 
        v.cell_id,
        v.cell_geom,
        s.id as station_id
    FROM voronoi v
    JOIN stations s ON ST_Contains(v.cell_geom, s.geom)
),
-- Clip each cell to the bounding box
clipped_cells AS (
    SELECT 
        cs.station_id,
        ST_Intersection(cs.cell_geom, b.geom) as clipped_geom
    FROM cell_station cs, bbox b
)
-- Calculate geodesic area in km² for each station's cell
SELECT 
    station_id,
    ST_Area(clipped_geom::geography) / 1000000.0 as area_km2
FROM clipped_cells
ORDER BY station_id
""")

cell_areas = pd.read_sql(query, engine)
print(cell_areas)

# Sum areas for roadside stations (14, 16, 17)
roadside_stations = [14, 16, 17]
roadside_total = cell_areas[cell_areas['station_id'].isin(roadside_stations)]['area_km2'].sum()
